correctness.rationale: The original mathematics checks out, but the surviving claim is specifically the rotation quotient's homotopy type. The repaired proof gives a closed-simplex injectivity argument for the regular quotient cell structure. The independent checker rebuilds the chord conflict graph and orbit incidences, checks 149 free-face collapses to (20,62,44), then contracts a 19-edge tree and eliminates 42 generator–disk pairs from the remaining 2-complex. The final signed words are a^-2 and the empty word. Substitution homotopes the other attaching maps in the subcomplex with the chosen disk; after substitution the singled-out edge and disk retract off the graph, preserving the two-complex's homotopy type. This is not an inference from the presentation of pi1 alone. The independent calculation also reproduced the original dihedral collapse to a point and all size 5–7 controls, but these are not part of the repaired finding.
residual_risks: Exact finite computation and standard CW arguments, not formal proof checking or a family theorem.

originality.rationale: The original compound claim fails originality as stated: the November 17 record already proves contractibility of the identical full dihedral quotient, computes the rotational H1, H2 and pi1, and establishes the torsion cutoff. The repair acknowledges this coverage and claims only the rotational wedge decomposition. The earlier chain reduction replaces chains algebraically, and its rotation presentation is of the two-skeleton with 42 three-cells still unaccounted for at the homotopy level. These prior calculations do not mechanically give the claimed wedge. The new collapse to a genuine 2-complex followed by the topological elimination of attaching loops establishes the surviving assertion.
residual_risks: Jonsson full text was not independently accessible. An unindexed equivalent description or a broader result outside the bounded checks can still exist. PASS applies to the repaired wedge classification only.

value.rationale: For the natural rotational quotient at the first known torsion-bearing polygon size, the wedge model supplies what was missing: an actual spherical summand realizing the free H2 class and a two-dimensional space with explicit attaching maps for the torsion. It is a complete homotopy description of a nontrivial canonical example, not a recomputation of known H1 or of the dihedral collapse.
residual_risks: No classification of larger polygons or other subgroups is claimed; the dihedral and small-polygon outputs serve as context or controls.
